desk.headline: HEPS up 102% to 4,439c as cheaper feed lifts poultry profit; revenue up 2.8% to R23.3bn; dividend doubled to 2,220c
results: HEPS more than doubled to 4,439c (up 102%) and EPS rose 98% to 4,502c, while revenue grew only 2.8% to R23.3bn.
The poultry division drove the jump: operating profit nearly tripled to R1.54bn and the margin rose to 7.9% from 2.8%.
Cheaper maize (down 23.4% to an average R3,485 a ton) cut feed costs; poultry prices rose 5.0% but sales volumes fell 2.0% as consumers cut back.
Feed division revenue fell 3.8% on lower selling prices, but volumes rose 6.3% and operating profit grew 13.8% to R812m.
Total dividend doubled to 2,220c (final 1,060c); cash rose to R1.44bn.

guidance.summary: Astral gives no earnings targets. It warns that higher fuel costs are squeezing household budgets, making it hard to pass on cost increases, and that El Nino threatens the summer grain crop, though the record 2026 harvest and its buying position may soften this. The financial impact of a strike at its Festive operations after year-end is not yet known.

points: CEO Gary Arnold called it a solid year helped by favourable trading conditions and fairly stable selling prices.
He said volume weakness was concentrated in the final quarter, as fuel costs left households less to spend on food.
Arnold said chicken imports fell to about 23% of local consumption from about 30% in 2019, crediting import tariffs and anti-dumping duties.
Management plans more value-added poultry capacity and says the balance sheet supports investment in efficiency and growth.
call.source: Business Day (23 Nov 2026) and Business Report (24 Nov 2026) coverage of the results

watch: The cost of the strike at the Festive poultry operations, which the company cannot yet measure.
Maize and feed prices if El Nino hurts the summer grain crop.
Whether chicken volumes recover as fuel costs squeeze consumer spending.
